c.tagline: Bangladesh's only coral island, a tiny Bay of Bengal outpost of coconut palms and reef-fringed beaches

rides: Walking, bicycle, or auto-rickshaw (the island is small)

taxi.fare: Negotiated flat rate for the short trips available
taxi.fareNote: The island is small enough to explore mostly on foot or by rented bicycle

emergency.note: Medical facilities on the island are very basic; serious emergencies require evacuation to the mainland

walk: The island is small enough to walk or cycle end to end in a couple of hours; there is no public transit

safety.safety: Generally safe, though facilities are basic and the island is remote; landing can be affected by monsoon-season sea conditions
safety.crime: Very low crime; the main risks are limited medical infrastructure and rough seas during the rainy season

hood_landmark.Main Village (Jetty Area): The island's jetty and main fishing village
hood_landmark.West Beach: The island's popular sunset-facing west beach
hood_landmark.Northern Coconut Groves: The island's quiet northern coconut palm groves

avoid.reason: Touts and overcharging cluster at the jetty, strong currents make some beaches risky, and overnight-stay limits are enforced in parts of the season.

hood_desc: The small settlement around the boat jetty, with most guesthouses, seafood shacks, and the local market.
A palm-lined stretch of beach on the island's west side, the best spot to watch the sunset over the Bay of Bengal.
A peaceful stretch of coconut groves on the island's quieter northern end, good for an escape from the jetty-area bustle.

water.note: Drink bottled water only; island supplies come from shallow wells and are untreated.

transit.sys: No formal transit; the island is explored on foot or by rented bicycle
transit.map: Not applicable given the island's small size
transit.note: The island is reached only by boat from Teknaf, and access can be restricted or suspended during the June-September monsoon season

transport.air: Cox's Bazar Airport (CXB), then a road and boat journey to the island
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Cox's Bazar or Teknaf
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect Dhaka and Chittagong to Teknaf (about 10-12 hr from Dhaka)
transport.ferry: Passenger boats and speedboats run from Teknaf to Saint Martin's Island (seasonal, weather-dependent)
transport.car: A car or bus reaches Teknaf; the final leg to the island is by boat only

airport.name: Cox's Bazar Airport (nearest gateway)
airport.distance: ~110 km (road) plus boat crossing from Teknaf
airport.transport: Bus or car to Teknaf, then boat to the island

net.m: Limited 3G/4G coverage, unreliable in parts of the island
net.w: Wifi available in a few resorts but limited
net.gb: ~$3-8 for a prepaid tourist SIM (best purchased on the mainland)
net.fwn: Wifi limited to a handful of resorts
net.ap: A Grameenphone or Robi prepaid SIM, purchased before crossing to the island

tip.s: Not customary but appreciated for boat operators and guides
tip.r: Not expected; rounding up is a nice gesture

food.name: Grilled Rupchanda and Coral Reef Fish
food.desc: Pick your fish off the ice, agree a price, and it is split, rubbed with spice and grilled over coals. Rupchanda pomfret and coral fish are the pick.

places.name: Beach barbecue stalls
places.note: Evening grills line the sand; fish is displayed on ice and cooked to order while you wait.

places.name: Sea Find Restaurant and Resort
places.note: Coastal dining with fresh seafood and sea views; a sit-down alternative to the beach grills.

places.name: Kather Bari Resort and Restaurant
places.note: Well-known island kitchen doing grilled and fried catch with rice; reliable for arrivals off the boat.

food.name: Grilled Lobster
food.desc: Bay of Bengal lobster split, buttered and grilled over charcoal. Saint Martin's is one of the few places in Bangladesh where it is a beachfront staple.

places.name: Beach barbecue stalls
places.note: Lobster laid out beside the fish each evening; price is agreed by size before cooking.

places.name: Blue Lagoon Beach Resort
places.note: Resort restaurant that prepares lobster and crab properly for guests and walk-ins.

places.name: Sea View Restaurant
places.note: Seafront kitchen doing grilled seafood plates with a view over the coral shelf.

food.name: Narikel Bhat (Coconut Rice)
food.desc: Rice cooked in the milk of the island's own coconuts until fragrant and slightly sweet, served under fish curry. Saint Martin's is called Narikel Jinjira.

places.name: Kather Bari Resort and Restaurant
places.note: Cooks island-style coconut rice alongside its seafood; a local dish rather than a mainland import.

places.name: Allahar Dan Restaurant
places.note: Straightforward Bangladeshi kitchen by the jetty serving rice, curry and coconut dishes cheaply.

places.name: Sea Find Restaurant and Resort
places.note: Serves coconut rice with the day's fish as a set plate for guests.

food.name: Coconut Prawn and Crab Curry
food.desc: Bay prawns or blue crab simmered in coconut milk with turmeric, ginger and green chilli into a mild, rich curry poured over rice.

places.name: Blue Lagoon Beach Resort
places.note: Does crab and prawn curries in coconut milk as well as grilled versions.

places.name: Sea View Restaurant
places.note: Local seafood curries at island prices; crab is best in the cooler months.

places.name: Dream Night Resort
places.note: Resort dining room serving coconut-milk seafood curries with sea views.

food.name: Shutki Bhuna
food.desc: Fish split and sun-dried on the island's racks, then fried hard with onion, garlic and chilli into a pungent, deeply savoury relish eaten with rice.

places.name: Saint Martin Bazar eateries
places.note: Small local rice hotels where islanders eat; shutki is everyday food rather than a tourist dish.

places.name: Allahar Dan Restaurant
places.note: Bangladeshi home-style cooking including dried-fish preparations at low prices.

places.name: Drying racks along the south beach
places.note: Where the shutki is made; walk past in the dry season to see the whole process.

food.name: Sea Fish Fry with Rice and Dal
food.desc: The island's everyday plate: whatever came ashore that morning, rubbed with turmeric and chilli, shallow-fried and served with rice, dal and a vegetable.

places.name: Saint Martin Bazar eateries
places.note: Basic rice hotels serving fried fish thalis all day for a fraction of resort prices.

places.name: Allahar Dan Restaurant
places.note: Popular quick meal for day-trippers between the boat and the beach.

places.name: Kather Bari Resort and Restaurant
places.note: Does the same plate in a slightly more comfortable setting.

food.name: Daab (Green Coconut Water)
food.desc: The island's name means coconut island, and green drinking nuts are cut open on every corner. Sweet, cold and the standard antidote to the sea heat.

places.name: Coconut sellers along the jetty road
places.note: Nuts cut open on the spot from morning until dark; the jelly is scooped out afterwards.

places.name: Saint Martin Bazar
places.note: Piles of daab sold beside the fruit stalls at the lowest prices on the island.

places.name: West beach shacks
places.note: Beach shacks sell chilled coconuts to sunset crowds along the western shore.

food.name: Doodh Cha (Island Milk Tea)
food.desc: Strong tea boiled with milk and plenty of sugar, poured from a battered kettle at the bazaar's tea stalls. The island's social ritual after dark.

places.name: Saint Martin Bazar tea stalls
places.note: Cluster of tea cabins where boatmen and shopkeepers gather every evening; cheap and constant.

places.name: Allahar Dan Restaurant
places.note: Serves milk tea with snacks for passengers waiting on the Teknaf boat.

places.name: Jetty road tea shops
places.note: First stop off the ferry; tea and biscuits while your bags are unloaded.

landmarks: Chera Dwip (Chhera Island)
The wild southern islet cut off at high tide, where coral outcrops, keya groves and dazzling clear water form Bangladesh's most pristine seascape.
West Beach
The island's sunset shoreline of coconut palms and coral-strewn sand, where fishing boats silhouette against blazing Bay of Bengal skies.
Coral Beach (East Beach)
A rugged eastern shore scattered with coral boulders and tide pools, delivering sunrise views across the turquoise shallows of Bangladesh's only coral island.
Shomudro Bilash (Humayun Ahmed's House)
The simple seafront retreat of beloved author Humayun Ahmed, a literary pilgrimage site where Bangladesh's greatest modern storyteller wrote beside the waves.
Saint Martin's Jetty
The island's bustling arrival pier, where ferries from Teknaf dock against a backdrop of fishing trawlers and impossibly blue water.
Narikel Jinjira Coconut Groves
The palm plantations that gave the island its Bengali name, Coconut Island, shading sandy lanes where fresh green coconuts are sold at every turn.
Coral Reefs and Snorkelling Shallows
The fringing reefs around the island's rocky points, home to living corals, colourful fish and Bangladesh's only true snorkelling and diving grounds.
Saint Martin's Bazaar
The lone market street near the jetty, fragrant with dried fish, grilled seafood stalls and the easygoing rhythms of island trading life.
Dakhinpara (Southern Village)
The island's quieter southern settlement of fishing families and coconut gardens, gateway to the tidal walk or boat ride across to Chera Dwip.
Keya Groves along the Shoreline
Dense belts of spiky screw-pine that armour the island's beaches against erosion, framing classic photographs of coral sand and emerald sea.

train.note: Saint Martin's is a small coral island in the Bay of Bengal with no railway of any kind. The nearest station is Cox's Bazar on the mainland, opened in December 2023 and served by Bangladesh Railway (https://eticket.railway.gov.bd/) with the Cox's Bazar Express and Parjatak Express from Dhaka via Chattogram. From there the island is reached only by ship, so a rail journey has to be combined with a boat.

bus.note: No road or bridge reaches the island and there are no buses on it - getting about is by battery-powered auto rickshaw, bicycle or on foot. Coaches from Dhaka (9-12 hours) and Chattogram (3-4 hours) run only as far as Cox's Bazar and Teknaf on the mainland, where the boats leave from; tickets for those are sold at operators' counters or online through Shohoz (https://www.shohoz.com/). Being an island, it has no international bus links.

intl.to: Cox's Bazar (Bangladesh) - ships from the BIWTA jetty at Nunia Chhara, about 5-6 hours each way
intl.op: Karnaphuli Cruise Line and other licensed operators

ferry.note: The island can only be reached by water. The traditional short run down the Naf River from Teknaf has been suspended because of the conflict on the Myanmar side of the river, leaving the longer open-sea crossing from Cox's Bazar as the only route. Sailings are seasonal, broadly November to January, and since 2025 the government has capped daily tourist numbers, restricted overnight stays and closed the island to visitors for much of the year, so check the rules and book before you travel. Rough seas and cyclone warnings can cancel departures at short notice.

half.name: Teknaf
half.blurb: The mainland port town roughly two to three hours away by boat is the departure point for the ferry to the island.

full.name: Cox's Bazar
full.blurb: A mainland beach city reached by boat and road in around five hours has the world's longest unbroken natural sea beach.
